But is it possible that the victory, which many consider to be a landslide, could have been an even bigger landslide had more advertising and attention been given to certain states?

It was close to being a near sweep like former President Ronald Reagan’s 1984 avalanche election against another vice president with a Minnesota connection – Walter Mondale – who, like Minnesota Governor Tim Walz (Harris’s choice for vice president), also hailed from the state.

Keep in mind that Trump only lost New Hampshire and Minnesota by 3 and 4 points respectively while traditionally solid blue states like New Jersey, New Mexico, and Virginia were all only 6 point losses for Trump.
He doubled his percentages in parts of New York City.

But the big question is this: Is it a coincidence that Harris only won states where there is no photo ID or strict voter identification requirements?
She lost every single state that had a photo ID requirement or strict ID requirements.
Can it make a difference?
You bet it can!
Here is a little history: I did not start out in politics running for Congress or the Senate.
I started by running for a position on the Republican Town Committee.
This position is the lowest of all the “political positions” in my state.
If your slate of nominees were challenged, you actually had an open election of all the Republicans in each district.
The unintended potential sinister use of “Get out the vote” can be implemented.
It could take the “door to door” canvassing to a dark place.
This is what I experienced.
I sat in the basement with about 30 or so other Republicans in similar roles.
The district chairman would painstakingly read off the names of each Republican on the voter rolls.
The nefarious goal was to identify who no longer lives in the district but is still on the voter rolls which were rarely purged or even reviewed.
Why is that important?
Well, if John Doe does not exist anymore, if he has moved or died, it does not mean that he cannot still vote.
Party leaders would note those folks, send out volunteers to verify if John Doe no longer exists and bingo, you got a new vote.
The party can replace John Doe with anyone they want. (Note both parties did it, so Democrats and Republicans only harvested their “own” votes.
After all, you cannot have two John Does showing up on Election Day).
Unfortunately, this illegal “art” has been perfected in certain inner-city communities and has been an established practice for decades.
Those states and the folks who reside in those states, and you know who you are, should demand photo ID and/or strict voter identification rules in order to vote.
Side note: Black Democratic leaders fought this practice for years claiming it was discriminatory (yeah, right).
Wonder why the inner-city vote was down in Atlanta, Detroit, Philadelphia, and Milwaukee?
The result: Trump won Georgia, Michigan, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin.
All those states now have photo ID or strict identification policies.
Coincidence?
I do not think so.
